common_name: Magnus Coneflower (Classic Flat Deep Rose-Purple Perennial Plant of the Year)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Magnus was named the 1998 Perennial Plant of the Year for its large, flat, deep rose-purple flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Magnus, named the 1998 Perennial Plant of the Year, bears large, single, deep rose-purple flowers with petals held unusually flat rather than drooping downward, a classic, widely imitated form that helped popularize coneflower as a mainstream garden perennial. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall, attracting bees, butterflies, and goldfinches that feed on the dried seed heads through winter. Deadhead to prolong bloom or leave seed heads standing for winter bird interest, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Kim's Mophead bears fully double white flowers with a dense, shaggy mass of small petaloids covering the entire center, giving each bloom a soft, pom-pom-like appearance that entirely obscures the usual spiny orange-bronze cone, on a notably compact plant that fits smaller borders. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall. Deadhead to prolong bloom, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Doubledecker is a curiosity heirloom coneflower producing a smaller secondary flower head sprouting directly atop the primary cone.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Doubledecker is a genuine botanical curiosity, an heirloom coneflower producing a small secondary flower head that sprouts directly from the top of the main cone, creating an odd, stacked, two-tiered bloom found in essentially no other widely grown perennial. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall and remains a favorite conversation piece among coneflower collectors. Deadhead to prolong bloom, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.

common_name: Razzmatazz Coneflower (Pioneering Fully Double Hot-Pink Pompom Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Razzmatazz was one of the first true fully double coneflowers introduced, bearing a dense hot-pink pompom with no visible cone.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Razzmatazz holds historical importance as one of the first true, stable, fully double coneflower cultivars ever introduced, bearing a dense, hot-pink pompom bloom with the central cone entirely replaced by a mass of small petaloids, a breakthrough form that opened the door to the many double coneflower cultivars bred since. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall. Deadhead to prolong bloom, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
